entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6834"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 115</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.115.1-Ps.115.18">Psa 115:1-18</reference>. The Psalmist prays that God would vindicate His glory, which is contrasted with the vanity of idols, while the folly of their worshippers is contrasted with the trust of God's people, who are encouraged to its exercise and to unite in the praise which it occasions.</title> <div sID="gen10494" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6834"/>1-3. The vindication of God's mercy and faithfulness (<reference osisRef="Ps.25.10">Psa 25:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.36.6">36:6</reference>) is the "glory" of His "name," which is desired to be illustrated in the deliverance of His people, as the implied mode of its manifestation. In view of the taunts of the heathen, faith in His dominion as enthroned in the heaven (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.4">Psa 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.11.4">11:4</reference>) is avowed. <div eID="gen10494" type="x-p"/>

In view of the taunts of the heathen, faith in His dominion as enthroned in the heaven ( Psa 2:4 ; 11:4 ) is avowed.
